statement: Every page of Lena's album has 4 stamps, and there are 12 stamps in all. She sticks 2 more stamps on every page. How many stamps are in the album now?

choices.misconception: I worked out how many pages the album has and stopped there.
I found how many stamps are on one page now, not in the whole album.
I gave the number of stamps before Lena stuck on any more.
I added just 2 stamps in all, but she adds 2 on every page.

hints: First find out how many pages there are.
12 stamps with 4 on each page tells you the number of pages. Every page gets 2 more stamps, so the number of new stamps depends on the number of pages.
There are 3 pages. Each page gets 2 more stamps, so 3 x 2 = 6 new stamps join the 12.

solutions.reliable: 12 stamps with 4 on each page fill 3 pages, because 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Each of the 3 pages gets 2 more stamps, which is 6 more stamps. The album now has 12 + 6 = 18 stamps. The idea to keep: when something happens on every page, first count how many pages there are.
solutions.elegant: After the new stamps, each page has 4 + 2 = 6 stamps. There are 3 pages, so 6 + 6 + 6 = 18. The idea to keep: find the new amount on one page, then count the pages.

whyOnTest: Finding what is asked: the hidden step is the number of pages, and adding 2 stamps only once is the trap.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
